summary: Iteration 8: end-to-end verification of the new Presets/FPS/Guide + Edit features. Backend: 10/10 pytest passed (test_presets_fps.py) — presets GET/PUT/reset (8 default frame rates, defaults.fps='50'), codecs auto-detected include MPEG-2 video and MP2 audio, stream create+edit+delete persists fps/resolution, channel create+edit persists fps/keyframe_s, channel with fps=25 starts successfully (has_master=true), engine/status returns frame_rates+ladders, profile PUT works, RBAC: scoped user gets 403 on PUT/POST reset presets but 200 on GET. UI (Playwright, admin): Mission Control loads; Presets page — added fps chip '100', Save Presets → reload → chip persisted; Reset restored defaults (chip gone). Streams — Create modal exposes separate Resolution + Frame Rate (fps) selects; edit button (edit-btn-<id>) opens prefilled modal; changing to 720p+25fps → PUT persists and row shows '720p@25'. Media Server New Channel modal has ch-fps + ch-keyframe + ch-ladder. Transcoding — 4 edit-profile-<id> buttons; new profile default ladder is '1080p50@6M / 720p50@3M / 576p25@1.2M' (p50/p25, no 60p). Guide page renders with 3 tabs (install/admin/user) in Russian, Скачать .md + PDF/Печать buttons present. All test data cleaned up.
critical_code_review_comments: Presets.jsx LadderEditor textarea uses defaultValue + onBlur only. If a user edits a ladder rung and clicks Save Presets before the textarea loses focus, the change won't be captured. Consider using value+onChange, or force blur() on Save.
Streams.jsx openCreate uses presets.resolutions[0] as default resolution (first item wins). Would be more predictable to add a defaults.resolution to presets rather than picking [0].

Guide.jsx builds the printable HTML with a simple esc() that handles & and <, but code:pre blocks receive the same escaping — acceptable but note user-typed content isn't involved here, so xss risk is low.

engine.build_cmd concatenates ',fps={fps}' to the scale filter; ensure fps is validated numeric (currently comes from a curated presets list which is fine, but PUT /api/config/presets accepts arbitrary strings — invalid entries like 'abc' would only fail at start_channel time).
